doc.title: John Beal interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2024

title: Playing Phantom of the Opera for years
summary: Beal explains how a player stays focused in a long Broadway run, and his 11-1/2 years on Phantom.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Interesting. Years ago I was able to sit in the orchestra pit of a production of “Cats” and I was watching, this was like a touring group, and I was watching the guys on the synthesizers, and they’d play their part and then they’d pick up a magazine, you know, and they would read, and then they’d put the magazine down and play their part. And I started to wonder, when you play a Broadway show for a length of time, sometimes years, how do you keep your focus? How do you not zone out and miss your cue?

Well you’re on automatic pilot you know. I mean it’s Broadway, you’re repeating eight shows a week if you do eight shows. But like I played “Phantom of the Opera” for 11-1/2 years but the contract on Broadway in New York you may send a sub for 50% of the shows. So I was able to work normal freelance stuff as well as the show. But you know where you are in the show. Some people would memorize their parts. I’ve never been able to separate that process, I always would read the part. But you know it depends on the quality of musicians in the result of the performance and I feel that that 50% rule made much better orchestras on Broadway because you’d get better players that are doing other things. And before that you’d be at the mercy of the conductor or contractor if you wanted to take off you know, they didn’t have to let you off so they’d get guys that the only thing they did was the show, grind it out you know.
